note: Human-reviewed list. The model never adds or edits entries. Every citation is a placeholder (verified:false) until a person checks it against the source; the UI marks it as not checked.

entries.title: Breathe slowly for 5 minutes right before your next Muse session.
entries.how: About 6 breaths a minute: in for 4 seconds, out for 6. The Muse breathing guide can pace it, or do it on your own.

evidence.summary: Slow breathing near 6 a minute raised heart-rate variability and lowered self-rated anxiety across small studies. Effects are short-term; long-term evidence is thinner.

sources.cite: Systematic review of slow breathing, 15 studies (Zaccaro 2018)

entries.title: Read for 10 minutes before a session.

evidence.summary: One small unpublished test. Shown as also considered, never suggested.

sources.cite: Reading before a session, 2009 unpublished test (rated weak)

entries.title: Take a 25-minute brisk walk outside before 5 PM.
entries.how: Brisk means you can talk but not sing. Outside beats a treadmill: you get the daylight too.

evidence.summary: Regular moderate activity improves sleep quality in large reviews.

sources.cite: 2018 US Physical Activity Guidelines Advisory Committee report

entries.title: Keep today's training easy: a walk or mobility, not intervals.
entries.how: Easy means effort under 10 on WHOOP. A hard day can wait until HRV is back near your usual.
entries.typeLabel: Easy day when HRV is low
entries.shortTitle: Easy training when HRV is under your usual

evidence.summary: Adjusting training to morning HRV gave similar or better fitness with fewer hard days in small trials.

entries.title: Decide the oldest waiting funding request before noon.
entries.how: Open Business, read the request, and decide. Amara won't decide for you.

evidence.summary: From your own ledger only. There's no outside science claim for business habits.

entries.title: Lights warm and dim after 9 PM.
entries.how: Switch the living room and bedroom to the warm evening scene yourself. Amara only suggests and checks.
entries.shortTitle: Lights warm and dim after 9 PM

evidence.summary: Bright room light in the evening delayed melatonin in a lab study; dimmer, warmer light did less.
